member.name: MarkdownRenderer.Remarks.EntryPoints
member.para: All entry points create and touch the toolkit's elements and must run on the UI thread that owns (or will own) the created elements. The theme's foreground and link brushes are applied directly, while the code and border brushes are derived from the surface background on first use; make a theme's brushes immutable so the theme can be built on a thread other than the one that creates and owns the elements.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.Remarks.Failures
member.para: Rendering failures are reported as warnings through when one is configured, and rendering then falls back to plain text; without a logger they are not reported. Hyperlink-open failures are reported as warnings as well and end the activation chain, but they do not affect the rendered content. A code-block language that is left to built-in resolution and finds no highlighting is reported through the logger at debug level when a logger is configured.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateContent.Remarks.Pipeline
member.para: The rendering pipeline is deliberately narrow: CommonMark plus pipe tables with GFM column alignment, strikethrough, and autolinks; HTML entity references such as & (the escaped source that displays as &) are decoded to their characters. Markdown constructs outside that set, including most other Markdig extensions, are not enabled and render as literal text; the package README lists the enabled and the unsupported constructs explicitly.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateContent.Remarks.HtmlAndImages
member.para: Raw HTML blocks and inline HTML are shown as literal text, and an image renders its alt text (or a muted placeholder when the alt text is empty) without loading the image. Whitespace-only content yields an empty plain-text element; an exception while parsing or rendering yields one that shows the content instead, and the exception is reported through the configured logger when one is set.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateContent.Remarks.Sizing
member.para: The returned viewer is left-aligned and clamped to and , so it sizes to its content instead of stretching to fill a host panel; center or stretch it from the host if a different placement is wanted.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateCodeBlockEditor.Remarks.CustomHighlighting
member.para: When configured, the custom highlighting callback is invoked before built-in resolution; see for the callback contract, including the ownership and cleanup of installed state. An exception thrown by the callback propagates to the caller.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateCodeBlockEditor.Remarks.Resolution
member.para: Built-in resolution tries the language as a highlighting definition name with the supplied casing, then case-insensitively against the registered definition names, then as a file extension, and finally through the aliases configured in , which default to an empty map. Definitions the editor engine does not ship (for example Lua or TypeScript) must be registered by the host or supplied through . The displayed text has its line endings normalized to line feeds and its conventional final terminator removed; authored trailing blank lines are preserved. The editor is read-only and does not accept keyboard focus; mouse selection and drag-and-drop follow and are disabled by default. The returned editor is host-owned, so a host can change it afterwards; it is the extension point for hosts that render code outside tooltip content.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateCodeBlockEditor.Remarks.HeightClamp
member.para: The returned editor is not height-clamped. When the renderer embeds a code block in tooltip content, the block is limited to visual lines and content beyond that scrolls, or is clipped when is .

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateCodeBlockEditor.Remarks.WheelRouting
member.para: Wheel routing is attached when and are enabled, so the host-owned editor scrolls itself and forwards an unconsumable wheel to its parent, exactly like a code block the renderer embeds. The scroll-bar visibility and the height clamp stay host-owned for a standalone editor.
